html:
Christianity is the religion based on the life and teaching of Jesus of Nazareth, whom Christians believe to be the Son of God, risen from the dead after his crucifixion around 30 CE. With more than two billion followers, it is the largest religion in the world.

It began as a movement within Judaism in Roman Judea. Paul and other missionaries spread it to non-Jews across the eastern Mediterranean, and by 200 CE there were churches in most cities of the Roman Empire. It grew in competition with other cults such as that of Mithras, and through times of crisis such as the Plague of Cyprian, when Christians cared for the sick.

After times of persecution, the emperor Constantine favoured it from 312, and in 380 it became the state religion of Rome. Councils such as Nicaea in 325 defined its creeds. It also spread beyond Rome, to Armenia, Ethiopia and Persia, and through the Church of the East to India and China.

Arguments over doctrine and power split it, above all the East-West Schism of 1054 between Catholic and Orthodox, and the Reformation from 1517, which created the Protestant churches. From the 1500s European empires and missionaries carried it across the Americas, Africa and Asia, and today most Christians live outside Europe.
